analysis_md:
# MOH — Molina Healthcare, Inc.
Pass 1 run, 2026-10-19. Price $207.05 (nasdaq_quote_api, dcf_numbers.json), market cap $10.953B — in scope under $40B.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Pure-play government managed care: Medicaid (the large majority of premium), Medicare dual-eligible products, and ACA Marketplace plans. ~4.9 million members at June 30, 2026, down 14% year over year on Medicaid market contraction, contract expirations and deliberate Marketplace shrinkage. SIC 6324 (Hospital & Medical Service Plans). It is exiting its traditional Medicare Advantage Part D product (~$1B premium) for 2027 and shrinking Marketplace by about $1B in 2027, while the new Florida Children's Medical Services Medicaid contract starts Q4 2026 (~$6B annual premium at full scale, with an expected start-up drag). Management calls 2026 the trough year for Medicaid margins and raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $5.25 in Q2 2026 (premium revenue guidance ~$42B, down from FY2025).

## Owner's earnings
- FY2025 (10-K): operating cash flow -$535,000,000; capex $101,000,000; SBC $47,000,000 → conservative OE -$683,000,000 = **-$12.91/share** (latest FY OE/share in dcf_numbers.json).
- FY2024: OCF $644,000,000, OE/share $7.42. FY2023: OCF $1,662,000,000, OE/share $25.18. OE positive 4 of the last 5 fiscal years (dcf_numbers.json).
- Maintenance definition and the OCF-based figure diverge widely year to year at a health plan because premiums, claims payable and amounts due to government agencies swing with settlement timing — the OCF-based conservative series is the one used, smoothed by the median (below).
- **Base used = normalized median of the last 3 FY OE/share: $7.42/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share; that is the FY2024 year sitting between FY2023's $25.18 and FY2025's -$12.91).
- **TTM (ttm.py through Q2 2026, quoted, not used as the base):** OCF: FY -$535,000,000 − prior YTD -$112,000,000 + current YTD $788,000,000 = TTM $365,000,000; capex TTM $94,000,000 (FY $101,000,000 − prior YTD $64,000,000 + current YTD $57,000,000); SBC TTM $76,000,000 (FY $47,000,000 − prior YTD $30,000,000 + current YTD $59,000,000); shares 51,200,000; **TTM OE total $195,000,000 → $3.81/share**. The TTM was rejected as the base: it is a trough figure (risk-corridor settlements and the MCR spike run through it, plus a $93M MAPD-exit impairment in H1 2026 operating results) — pinning the base to the trough and then growing it would treat a rate/trend trough management and the rate cycle are expected to correct as the permanent earning power. The deterioration the TTM shows is instead carried in the recalibrated growth starts, the 0.75/0.90 bear multipliers and the widened bear weight below. Method range: on the TTM base the same scenarios would score materially lower (roughly half the IV); on the preliminary engine growth (15.71% start) the median base scored 9.70% weighted IRR / Tier D — every defensible variant is Tier D at $207.05.
- Balance sheet (FY2025, fundamentals.json / dcf_numbers.json): cash $4,248,000,000 plus short-term investments $4,008,000,000, total debt $3,766,000,000, equity $4,069,000,000; **net debt -$482,000,000 (net cash)**, net debt / normalized OE -1.23x. Note much of the cash and investments sits in regulated subsidiaries held against medical claims and government liabilities — it is not all distributable parent cash (parent cash was ~$223M at Dec 31, 2025 per the FY2025 release); days in claims payable 47.

## Moat: 4/10 — weak to moderate
Justification: pure-play government-programs expertise, incumbency and a low cost base, but no pricing power (states/CMS set rates), rebid risk on every contract, contracted (not owned) providers, and subscale versus the diversified payers.
- FOR: ~8% national Medicaid share and expertise in complex, high-acuity populations; multi-year state contracts with an RFP track record (Illinois retained, Wisconsin renewed, Florida CMS won — ~$6B annual premium at full scale); G&A ratio 6.5% in FY2025, a focused-footprint cost advantage; integrated dual-eligible offering aligned with policy direction.
- AGAINST: no pricing power — 2026 Medicaid MCR guided 92.9% because rates lagged 5% medical trend; contracts are rebid and losable (membership -14% YoY); subscale vs UnitedHealthcare/Elevance/Centene; providers contracted, not owned; effectively all revenue is government premium, exposed to redeterminations, ACA subsidy expiry and state budgets.
- Return evidence (fundamentals.json): gross margin (1 minus MCR) 15.9% FY2023 → 15.3% FY2024 → 13.1% FY2025; operating margin 4.6% → 4.2% → 1.7%. The roic_proxy series is not meaningful for this balance sheet — it divides by equity + debt − cash only, so regulated cash/investments held against claims liabilities drive it to absurd levels (10.94 in FY2020, 0.17 in FY2025) — the margin series is the usable evidence and it does not support a moat above 4.
- A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 7.2 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-19)
**Growth recalibration (written reason, mandatory sanity check):** the engine's blended start is 15.71% (5-yr revenue CAGR 18.52%, 3-yr 12.41%, latest YoY 11.75%, plus a +3.30pp buyback adjustment). That describes the pre-2026 expansion, not the current prints: TTM revenue growth is +2.55% (fundamentals.json), Q2 2026 total revenue fell ~5% YoY and premium revenue ~6%, membership is -14%, and FY2026 premium guidance is ~$42B (down). Scenario starts were therefore set via offsets (-0.2171 / -0.1771 / -0.1371 / -0.0871 / -0.0371 vs g_base) to -6% / -2% / **+2%** / +7% / +12%. The super-bull +12% start is the only one near the FY2025 print (+11.75%) and is justified only by the Florida CMS ramp (~$6B at full scale) plus a full rate/trend correction — it is deliberately the lowest-probability case. Probabilities 15/30/30/15/10 (bear weight widened per OE_VOLATILE); OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | -6.0% | 0.75 | Rates keep lagging trend; more contract/membership loss | $32.77 | 4.31% |
| Bear | 30% | -2.0% | 0.90 | 2026 guided contraction persists; MCR stuck ~93% | $46.00 | 5.17% |
| Base | 30% | +2.0% | 1.00 | Trough margins, flat-to-low growth, gradual rate catch-up | $59.67 | 6.09% |
| Bull | 15% | +7.0% | 1.10 | Rate correction lands 2027; Florida CMS ramps cleanly | $79.48 | 7.43% |
| Super bull | 10% | +12.0% | 1.25 | Full margin recovery toward the 2029 target path | $109.04 | 9.34% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $59.44 (-71.3% vs price), IV@12% $78.30, IV@10% $99.27, weighted IRR 6.10%, base-case IRR 6.09%**
- **Tier by numbers: D** (bear D 5.17%, bull D 7.43% — even the super-bull case, 9.34%, does not reach Tier C). Diagnostics: OE yield 3.58%, terminal value 17.9% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.33x, net debt -1.23x normalized OE, 9.6 months since FY end.
- Hurdle prices: clears 15% at $59.44, 20% at $42.39, 25% at $32.93.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended 10 months ago): resolved by running ttm.py — TTM OE is $3.81/share on the legs quoted above (OCF $365M, capex $94M, SBC $76M, shares 51.2M). The TTM is disclosed and deliberately not pinned as the base, for the trough reason given under Owner's earnings; the final run therefore uses the normalized median base with trough conditions carried in growth, multipliers and probabilities.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY OE/share -$12.91 vs 3-yr median $7.42): the latest FY is the distorted one on the cash-flow leg — FY2025 OCF was -$535M against net income of $472M, driven (per the FY2025 release and Q3 2025 cash-flow statement) mainly by Medicaid risk-corridor settlement activity (amounts due government agencies fell $467M in the first nine months), the timing of tax payments, and lower second-half operating performance. The earnings leg also genuinely deteriorated (operating income $781M vs $1,707M in FY2024 as MCR rose), which is why the median is used only with trough growth/multiplier adjustments rather than at face value.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (>40% in 2024 and 2025): same mechanism in both directions — 2024 OCF $644M vs net income $1,179M and 2025 OCF -$535M vs net income $472M, i.e. risk-corridor / amounts-due-government settlements, Marketplace risk-transfer payments, claims-payable timing (medical claims and benefits payable -$157M in 9M 2025) and tax-payment timing, per the company's cash-flow statements and earnings commentary. No impairment or tax-deposit one-off explains the gap; it is settlement/working-capital timing inherent to government health plans, and it is the reason the 3-yr median, not any single year, is the base.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3x over 5 years: $29.50 / $33.62 / $9.90 / $25.18 / $7.42 / -$12.91 on the filed history): real and structural for this payer (settlement timing plus MCR cycles). Handled as the flag directs — normalized median base and bear weight widened to 45% on bear-or-worse (15% super bear + 30% bear vs the 35% default).
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count shrinking 3.3%/yr): already credited via the +3.30pp growth adjustment inside the engine blend (and the recalibrated starts are offsets from that blend, so the credit carries through); not double-counted in the verdict. Molina repurchased $1,000,000,000 of stock in FY2025 (fundamentals.json); the H1 2026 quarterly rows show no buybacks.
- Preliminary-run flags that no longer fire on the final run: WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD (spread is now 3.33x, below the flag threshold — uncertainty is still wide in absolute terms, and confidence is low regardless) and TIER_BAND (bear, base and bull are all Tier D on the final inputs, so there is no tier span to size against; the verdict is D on every scenario).

## Thoughts / method range
- This is an insurer-style cash-flow series run through an OCF-minus-capex model: single years are close to meaningless (OE/share has printed both $33.62 and -$12.91 within five years), so the honest headline is the range. Preliminary engine inputs (median base, 15.71% growth): 9.70% weighted IRR. Final recalibrated inputs: 6.10%. A TTM-base variant would be lower still. All variants are Tier D — the tier is robust, the exact IRR is not.
- The investment debate is really about the 2027-29 margin recovery (management's path leans on ~90bp of Medicaid MCR improvement and a $25 EPS target for 2029). Even granting the super-bull version of that recovery as the *expected* case, the IRR at $207.05 is only 9.34% — the price already pays for the recovery.
- Quality watch items: S&P downgraded the senior notes to BB- in April 2026; debt-to-capital 47% at Q2 2026; the Florida CMS start-up drag ($1.50/share guided burden in 2026, including MAPD underperformance) and the Marketplace risk-adjustment drag are guided, not hypothetical.
- Confidence is **low**: OE volatility, settlement-timing noise in every base candidate, and a verdict that depends on a state rate cycle the company does not control.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 6.10% on the final inputs; bear 5.17%, bull 7.43%, super bull 9.34%)
- Confidence: **Low**
- One-liner: Weak-moat (4/10) government managed-care payer in a rate/trend trough — normalized owner's earnings are $7.42/share but at $207.05 the weighted IRR is only 6.1% (IV@15% $59.44); it clears the 15% hurdle only at or below ~$59.
